The Commonwealth of Kentucky relies heavily on fossil fuels, and our coal resources provide our state thousands of jobs and deliver over 83% of our electricity. Trump Approves Kentucky FEMA Funds After Barr, Congressional Delegation Push for Approval | Press Releases | Congressman Andy Barr Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Print Trump Approves Kentucky FEMA Funds After Barr, Congressional Delegation Push for Approval September 1 , 2026 Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Congressman Andy Barr (R-KY-06) applauded President Donald Trump for approving $9.1 million in Public Assistance (PA) relief through the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to Kentucky for severe weather impacting Kentuckians earlier this year from June 17-30. The President announced the approval via TruthSocial earlier tonight. Kentuckians in these counties are eligible for PA under the FEMA designation: Bullitt, Butler, Clinton, Cumberland, Garrard, Grayson, Green, Hardin, Henderson, Jackson, Jessamine, Madison, Meade, Mercer, Metcalfe, Ohio, Owsley, Rockcastle, Spencer, and Wayne. Congressman Barr led the Kentucky Congressional Delegation in urging an approval of the FEMA request from Kentucky earlier this year in a letter to the President. “I just informed Andy Barr that I am approving 9.1 Million Dollars for severe storms, winds, flooding, landslides, and mudslides, that they are recovering from. The Great People of Kentucky are resilient, smart, and tough, and I am with them all the way,” President Trump said in-part. “Tonight, I spoke with President Trump over the phone. I am grateful that after I advocated for FEMA relief to recover from difficult storms that hit Kentucky earlier this summer, President Trump is approving $9.1M in federal funds to Kentucky,” said Congressman Barr. “I will always fight to deliver for the people of our Commonwealth.” ### Permalink: https://barr.house.gov/2026/9/trump-approves-kentucky-fema-funds-after-barr-congressional-delegation-push-for-approval Press Releases Photo Gallery Newsletters Video Gallery

Barr Reintroduces Bill to Fix Failed Housing Policy | Press Releases | Congressman Andy Barr Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Print Barr Reintroduces Bill to Fix Failed Housing Policy October 3 , 2025 Washington, D.C.— This week, U.S. Congressman Andy Barr (R-KY), a senior member of the House Financial Services Committee, has reintroduced the Housing Promotes Livelihood and Ultimate Success (Housing PLUS) Act, aimed at reforming the Department of Housing and Urban Development’s (HUD) exclusive reliance on the so-called “Housing First” methodology. Specifically, this bill directs the HUD Secretary to prioritize Continuum of Care (CoC) funding for providers that require wraparound services such as job training and addiction treatment, as well as for faith-based organizations. It mandates that no less than 50% of CoC funding be allocated to recipients that provide or facilitate access to these recovery-focused services. The bill also requires the Secretary to certify annually to Congress that HUD funding has been distributed accordingly, and to report on how allocations met these requirements. “Those struggling with homelessness need housing PLUS services,” said Congressman Barr . “Up until 2013, HUD funded critical wraparound services in conjunction with housing to ensure homeless individuals break the cycle of homelessness permanently. The Housing PLUS Act ensures federal funds are reaching providers who are helping people transition from homelessness to self-sufficiency, without unneeded restrictions.” “If we want to curb homelessness, we need to ensure that the service providers reaching this population can also help meet housing needs,” said Congressman Mike Flood (R-NE), Chairman of the House Financial Services Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance . “The Housing PLUS Act helps take a more integrated approach and scraps the failed Housing First philosophy used

Barr Calls Out Beshear Over Inaccurate Rural Hospital Claims | Press Releases | Congressman Andy Barr Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Print Barr Calls Out Beshear Over Inaccurate Rural Hospital Claims August 25 , 2026 WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Congressman Andy Barr (R-KY-06) called on Governor Andy Beshear to explain why his administration’s $212.9 million federal rural health plan does not clearly identify or prioritize the 35 Kentucky hospitals Beshear repeatedly claimed would close because of H.R. 1. In a letter to Governor Beshear, Barr highlighted the discrepancy between the Governor’s repeated public warnings and his administration’s recently announced plan for $212.9 million in federal funding through the Rural Health Transformation Program . For months, Beshear has told Kentuckians that 35 rural hospitals were at risk because of the legislation. On June 23, 2025, he stated that “35 rural hospitals in Kentucky will close.” Days later, Beshear warned that “35 hospitals are under the threat of closing, stripping care from families, cutting jobs and crippling local economies.” He later claimed Congress had voted to “close 35 rural hospitals in our state” and has continued repeating these claims dozens of times. However, the Sheps Center analysis associated with the 35-hospital figure never concluded that 35 Kentucky hospitals would close. The analysis identified financially vulnerable hospitals from across the country but did not conclude that those hospitals would close because of H.R. 1. Senate Democrats later used their own selected criteria to identify 35 Kentucky hospitals as being at increased risk, but neither the Sheps analysis nor the Senators’ list concluded that those hospitals would close. Kentucky Congressional Delegation Urges President Trump to Approve Kentucky’s Major Disaster Declaration | Press Releases | Congressman Andy Barr Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Print Kentucky Congressional Delegation Urges President Trump to Approve Kentucky’s Major Disaster Declaration July 28 , 2026 Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Congressman Andy Barr (R-KY-06) led the Kentucky Congressional Delegation in urging President Donald J. Trump to swiftly approve the Commonwealth of Kentucky’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration following the devastating storms, flooding, tornadoes, and severe weather that struck communities across the Commonwealth between June 17 and June 30. The delegation’s letter expresses strong support for the Commonwealth’s request and asks for immediate federal assistance to help Kentucky families and communities recover. The prolonged weather event caused widespread damage across Kentucky, claiming the lives of six Kentuckians, including three residents of Madison County, while destroying homes, damaging businesses, washing out roads and bridges, and leaving thousands without power. Nineteen counties and thirteen cities declared states of emergency as multiple rounds of severe weather compounded the damage over nearly two weeks. The Commonwealth formally requested a Major Disaster Declaration on July 23. “Kentucky families have endured an extraordinary stretch of severe weather, and many communities are facing a long road to recovery,” said Congressman Barr. “The damage across Central Kentucky, especially in Madison County where lives were tragically lost and neighborhoods were devastated, underscores the urgent need for federal assistance. Barr Votes to Strengthen America’s Military, Support Servicemembers, and Confront Global Threats | Press Releases | Congressman Andy Barr Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Print Barr Votes to Strengthen America’s Military, Support Servicemembers, and Confront Global Threats July 22 , 2026 Washington, D.C. — Congressman Andy Barr (R-KY) voted today in favor of the Fiscal Year 2027 National Defense Authorization Act, legislation that strengthens America’s military, supports servicemembers and their families, and ensures the United States is prepared to confront growing threats around the world. The legislation delivers a 5% to 7% pay raise for America’s servicemembers, invests more than $11.7 billion through the Pacific Deterrence Initiative to counter Communist China, strengthens America’s defense industrial base, and improves military readiness. The bill also reinforces America’s support for Israel, strengthens cooperation against shared threats in the Middle East, and ensures the United States and its allies have the capabilities necessary to confront Iran and its terrorist proxies. “America must lead from a position of strength,” said Congressman Barr. “This legislation includes a much deserved pay raise for the men and women who defend our nation, strengthens our ability to deter Communist China, stands firmly with our ally Israel, and ensures we are prepared to confront Iran and its terrorist proxies. It also invests in American workers, manufacturers, and innovators so our military remains the most capable fighting force in the world. Peace through strength requires a ready military, a strong defense industrial base, and an unwavering commitment to our allies.” The FY27 NDAA: Delivers a 5% to 7% pay raise for servicemembers and continues investments in military housing, childcare, and quality-of-life programs for military families. Barr Introduces Lawful Hemp Protection Act to Protect Kentucky Farmers, Consumers, and the Future of the Hemp Industry | Press Releases | Congressman Andy Barr Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Print Barr Introduces Lawful Hemp Protection Act to Protect Kentucky Farmers, Consumers, and the Future of the Hemp Industry July 22 , 2026 Washington, D.C. – Today, U.S. Congressman Andy Barr (R-KY-06) introduced the Lawful Hemp Protection Act, bipartisan legislation to establish the first comprehensive federal regulatory framework for hemp-derived consumer products while protecting Kentucky farmers, enhancing consumer and child safety, and preserving the long-term viability of the domestic hemp industry. This legislation establishes a clear federal framework for the hemp industry by setting consistent standards for cultivation, manufacturing, testing, and labeling, while prohibiting synthetic cannabinoids in finished hemp-derived products. It also supports American farmers by only allowing hemp grown, cultivated, and packaged in the United States. To further strengthen consumer protection and child safety, Rep. Barr’s legislation limits retail sales of hemp-derived consumer products to individuals 21 years of age and older and prohibits the marketing or advertisement of any hemp products towards children. “Kentucky farmers helped build America’s hemp industry and they deserve certainty,” said Congressman Barr . “The Lawful Hemp Protection Act protects Kentucky agriculture, safeguards consumers, and establishes a commonsense regulatory framework that allows this important industry to continue to grow while ensuring products are safe and kept out of the hands of children. Kentucky has demonstrated that hemp can be successfully regulated while supporting farmers and protecting consumers. Barr Leads House Passage of Main Street Capital Access Act to Strengthen Community Banks and Expand Opportunity | Press Releases | Congressman Andy Barr Facebook Icon Google Plus Icon Instagram Icon LinkedIn Icon Twitter Icon YouTube Icon Vimeo Icon Clients Icon Email icon Map Icon Print Icon Quote Icon icon_share Carousel Arrow - Left Carousel Arrow - Right Skip Navigation Press Releases Home Media Center Press Releases Print Barr Leads House Passage of Main Street Capital Access Act to Strengthen Community Banks and Expand Opportunity July 21 , 2026 WASHINGTON, D.C. —Congressman Andy Barr (R-KY-06), Chairman of the House Financial Services Subcommittee on Financial Institutions, applauded House passage of the Main Street Capital Access Act , legislation to strengthen community banks, expand access to credit, and support families, farmers, and small businesses across Kentucky. The legislation modernizes outdated banking regulations that have made it harder for community banks to grow and compete. By reducing unnecessary regulatory burdens and encouraging the formation of new community banks, the bill helps preserve a competitive financial system while expanding access to capital on Main Street. Subcommittee Chairman Barr said, "Community banks are at the heart of Kentucky's economy. They finance our small businesses, stand by our farmers, and help hardworking families buy homes, start businesses, and build a better future. House Republicans are delivering on our commitment to strengthen Main Street by cutting red tape, expanding access to capital, and creating an environment where community banks can thrive. I'm grateful to Chairman French Hill for his leadership, and I'm proud the House is advancing this legislation to support the local financial institutions that keep our communities strong."
